title: FTSE Russell — preliminary June 2027 additions/deletions published after 6 p.m. ET (five weeks before implementation)
source: EST: rule-derived from the index owner's ground rules and confirmed against FOUR consecutive published instances of the five-week convention. GROUND RULES, re-fetched and text-extracted independently this session (2026-09-06): FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026 (lseg.com dam PDF, HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, 77 content streams inflated in-session, 277,404 characters extracted; the cover's own version string reads "August 2026 Construction and Methodology ... v7.2"). Appendix F's June column: Preliminary Information Released = "Five weeks prior to implementation", Query Period = "For two weeks following preliminary announcement", Lock down = "Three weeks after query period ends", Implementation = "4th Friday of June"; section 4.3.1 repeats it verbatim -- changes "are announced five weeks prior to implementation for the June review and four weeks prior to the December review"; and the same appendix defines Rank Day: "The Rank Day occurs on the last business day of April for the June reconstitution and the last business day of October for the December reconstitution." The schedule is internally consistent (5 weeks prelim = 2 weeks query + 3 weeks lockdown). June 2027's implementation is Friday 2027-06-25 (see russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25.json for the two-clause derivation and its 36-of-36-year proof), so five weeks prior is Friday 2027-05-21 and the query period ends Friday 2027-06-04. THE CONVENTION IS NOT ASSUMED -- it is confirmed against every June the owner has published a schedule for since the current regime began, each read this session off FTSE Russell's own schedule press release for that year: 2023 prelim 05-19 -> impl 06-23 (35 days), 2024 prelim 05-24 -> impl 06-28 (35 days), 2025 prelim 05-23 -> impl 06-27 (35 days), 2026 prelim 05-22 -> impl 06-26 (35 days, and stated a second time on lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution -- HTTP 200, 228,333 bytes, 13,561 characters extracted -- as "following the publication of preliminary lists beginning on May 22", and a third time in the owner's June 2026 reconstitution summary PDF as "The preliminary membership changes announced on May 22, 2026"). Four instances, four exact matches. THE FIVE-WEEK WINDOW IS ONLY FOUR YEARS OLD, which this entry records because it bounds every historical study of it: 2019-2022 ran a THREE-week window off a May rank day (2019 prelim 06-07 -> impl 06-28, 2020 06-05 -> 06-26, 2021 06-04 -> 06-25, 2022 06-03 -> 06-24, all 21 days), and the April rank day plus the five-week announcement arrived together in 2023. Filed estimate because no FTSE Russell 2027 reconstitution calendar exists yet -- the owner has published its schedule press release in early March each year (2023-03-01, 2025-03-03, 2026-03-02), so the 2027 calendar is not due until roughly 2027-03; this is an unpublished document, not a blocked fetch. Promote on that published 2027 schedule naming the preliminary date. Discovered during the russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 initial research; canonical file written and every clause above re-verified from the primaries during this event's own initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: THE INFORMATION EVENT, where 2027-06-25 is the EXECUTION event: this is when the membership changes and the indicative shares-outstanding and free-float data become public, five weeks before any share moves. The ground rules define the release as "preliminary additions, deletions, indicative shares outstanding and free float data" -- weights, not just names. It is PRELIMINARY in the owner's own operative sense: a two-week query period runs to 2027-06-04 during which "FTSE Russell welcomes queries on the published data" and the lists are revised each Friday, and only at lock-down (Monday 2027-06-07, the convention confirmed against 2023-06-05 / 2024-06-10 / 2025-06-09 / 2026-06-08) is the reconstitution "considered final". MEASURED THIS SESSION, and the measurement is why impact is low: across the eight years whose announcement date is sourced from the owner's own schedule (2019-2026), the announcement-to-implementation window is a NULL on IWM-vs-SPY total return -- mean -0.01%, one-sided bootstrap p=42% against an unconditional -0.24%; the five-week sub-sample's +0.61% mean is one year (2026's +7.39%) carrying a -0.44% median. The announcement is also NOT a volume event: IWM whole-day volume on the first tradeable session printed BELOW its own trailing-60d median in 8 of 8 years (0.59x-1.02x, median 0.90x), against the 1.42x the implementation session runs. One result did survive -- IWM-vs-SPY on that first tradeable session averaged +0.64%, 7 of 8 positive, bootstrap p=0.8% -- and it is registered as a forward test rather than believed: 61% of it is the overnight gap (+0.39%, 7/8) that can only be captured by holding small-caps long into an unpublished list, the tradeable-on-the-published-list remainder is +0.25% at 5 of 8, one of six shifted-Friday placebos also cleared p<0.05, and the edge is gone by five sessions (p=87%). Lists post AFTER 6 p.m. ET, so nothing is tradeable on the announcement Friday itself. Status estimate, impact low, no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-06: zero hits), shorting is blocked house-wide -- this widens caution and licenses nothing. NOTE FOR 2027 SPECIFICALLY: 2027-05-21 is also monthly opex (opex-2027-05-21, tracked), so any 2027 announcement-day volume or flow read is confounded at the source.
